# `krishiv.sql.readwriter`

<!-- @generated by `python3 tests/scripts/gen_python_docs.py`; do not edit. -->

`DataFrameReader` (`spark.read`), `DataFrameWriter` (`df.write`)
and `DataFrameWriterV2` (`df.writeTo`).

The format and path are checked when the query is analyzed; save modes are
checked by the engine (`SaveMode::parse`), so the writer passes the mode
string through unchanged.

## `DataFrameWriter`

```python
class DataFrameWriter
```

Writes a :class:`DataFrame`'s rows to files (a subset of
`pyspark.sql.DataFrameWriter`: `format`/`mode`/`option`/
`options`/`partitionBy`/`bucketBy`/`sortBy`/`save`/
`saveAsTable`/`insertInto` and the `parquet`/`csv`/`json`/`text`
shortcuts). `bucketBy` and `sortBy` are accepted but the engine has no
bucketed tables: `save` and `insertInto` fail as in Spark and
`saveAsTable` with `KRISHIV_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`; so does writing `orc`.
`saveAsTable` in `overwrite` mode drops and recreates the table (a query
reading it fails with `UNSUPPORTED_OVERWRITE.TABLE`) and `insertInto` in
`overwrite` mode is `INSERT OVERWRITE`. Unknown formats fail the
same way and unknown modes with `INVALID_SAVE_MODE`.

### `bucketBy`

```python
def bucketBy(self, numBuckets: int, col: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...], *cols: str) -> DataFrameWriter
```

Buckets the output by `col` (and `cols`) into `numBuckets`
buckets. Only `saveAsTable` accepts it in Spark, and the engine has
no bucketed tables (see the class doc).

### `csv`

```python
def csv(self, path: str, mode: str | None=None, partitionBy: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None=None, **options: object) -> None
```

### `format`

```python
def format(self, source: str) -> DataFrameWriter
```

### `insertInto`

```python
def insertInto(self, tableName: str, overwrite: bool | None=None) -> None
```

Inserts the rows into the existing table `tableName` by position.

```

```

### `partitionBy`

```python
def partitionBy(self, *cols: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...]) -> DataFrameWriter
```

Names of columns to partition by; each call replaces the columns of
the one before. Only column names (`str`) are
accepted; `Column` objects raise a type error. The engine writes no
partitioned layout, so any column fails `save` with
`KRISHIV_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`; an empty `partitionBy` is a no-op,
as in Spark.

### `save`

```python
def save(self, path: str | None=None, format: str | None=None, mode: str | None=None, partitionBy: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None=None, **options: object) -> None
```

### `saveAsTable`

```python
def saveAsTable(self, name: str, format: str | None=None, mode: str | None=None, partitionBy: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None=None, **options: object) -> None
```

Saves the rows as the table `name` (`errorifexists` fails on an
existing table, `ignore` leaves it, `append` adds by column name).

### `sortBy`

```python
def sortBy(self, col: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...], *cols: str) -> DataFrameWriter
```

Sorts each bucket by `col` (and `cols`); needs `bucketBy`.

### `text`

```python
def text(self, path: str, compression: str | None=None, lineSep: str | None=None) -> None
```

Writes the rows as text files: one string column, as in Spark.

## `DataFrameWriterV2`

```python
class DataFrameWriterV2
```

Writes a :class:`DataFrame`'s rows to a table (a subset of
`pyspark.sql.DataFrameWriterV2`: `using`/`option`/`options`/
`tableProperty`/`partitionedBy`/`clusterBy` and the `create`/
`replace`/`createOrReplace`/`append`/`overwrite`/
`overwritePartitions` actions).

Only collection happens here; the engine (`krishiv-session`'s
`DataFrameWriterV2`) runs the request through the same command path
SQL uses (`CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and friends), so
`writeTo("t").create()` and `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT ...` run one
code path. `create` fails on an existing table with
`TABLE_OR_VIEW_ALREADY_EXISTS`; `append` is `INSERT INTO` by
position. File-source tables cannot be replaced, so `replace` and
`createOrReplace` fail as `REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT` does
(`UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.TABLE_OPERATION`); `overwrite` and
`overwritePartitions` always fail with `KRISHIV_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`
naming `INSERT OVERWRITE`; partitioned or clustered
tables fail the same way, as `CREATE TABLE ... PARTITIONED BY` does.

### `append`

```python
def append(self) -> None
```

### `clusterBy`

```python
def clusterBy(self, col: str, *cols: str) -> DataFrameWriterV2
```

Names of columns to cluster by; each call replaces the columns of
the one before. Only column names (`str`) are accepted. The engine
runs no clustered tables yet, so any column fails `create` with
`KRISHIV_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`; `append` ignores them.

```python

```

### `overwrite`

```python
def overwrite(self, condition: Column | str) -> None
```

Overwrites the rows `condition` selects. This always fails with
`KRISHIV_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` naming `INSERT OVERWRITE`; the condition (a
:class:`Column` or SQL text) never runs.
